guideTitle: Texas Hold’em, from the first card to the pot.
guideIntro: A visual guide to getting started with friends. All chips here are virtual.
handsIntro: From the strongest hand to the simplest, with examples you can consult while playing.
helpIntro: Answers about Highlords and a glossary to understand the table talk.
goal: You receive two private cards and share five community cards. Use zero, one or two of your own cards to form your best five-card hand. You also win the pot if everyone else folds.
exampleOnly: TEACHING EXAMPLE · NOT A LIVE GAME
formatsTitle: Cash game, Sit & Go or tournament?
formats: Cash games have fixed blinds and top-ups under room rules. A Sit & Go runs on one table with rising blinds. Multi-table tournaments distribute and rebalance players across tables. In both tournament formats, the last player with chips is the champion.
rankingNote: Strongest first. Examples show five cards; during play, your best five-card combination counts. Suits have equal value.
ties: Compare the category first, then the card values that make the hand. A kicker breaks a tie when it belongs to the best five cards. Identical best five-card hands split the pot; sixth and seventh cards do not count. An ace can be high in 10-J-Q-K-A or low in A-2-3-4-5, but straights cannot wrap around. One flush never beats another because of its suit.
tryBody: Create a room, add bots or invite friends. You decide when to start.
beforeFlop: Your five-card combination becomes available from the flop.
foldedTip: You folded this hand. Your cards remain private; wait for the next hand.
handOverTip: The hand has ended. Check the result and wait for the next deal.
callTip: Calling {{amount}} chips keeps you in this hand. Raising increases the bet; folding gives up your claim to the pot.
checkTip: You can check without adding chips, or place a bet.
watchTip: Your controls appear on your turn. Use only your cards and the community board to evaluate your hand.
finalResult: The final result is recorded. All prizes are virtual.
finalHint: Full standings are in the players panel. Export the record from room options.
coachingNotice: Help uses only your cards and the board. It does not calculate odds or read opponents.
step0Body: The D button marks the dealer. Small and big blinds are forced bets. Heads-up, the button posts the small blind and acts first before the flop.
step1Body: You hold A♠ and K♥. There are no community cards yet. Action starts left of the big blind, except heads-up. Call, raise or fold when it is your turn.
step2Body: Three cards are revealed: A♦, 7♣ and 2♥. You now have a pair of aces. After the flop, the first active player left of the button acts first.
step3Body: K♠ is the fourth community card. In this example, you improve to two pair: aces and kings. Another betting round follows.
step4Body: 9♦ completes the board. Your best hand is A♠ A♦ K♥ K♠ 9♦. This is the last betting round; no more community cards will be dealt.
step5Body: If more than one player remains, eligible hands are compared. Two pair loses to three of a kind or any higher category. If everyone folds to you, you win without showing. All-ins can create side pots: each player contests only the pots they contributed to.
rank0Body: No pair or other combination. Compare the five cards in order.
rank1Body: Two cards of the same rank and three kickers.
rank2Body: Two different pairs and a kicker.
rank3Body: Three cards of the same rank and two kickers.
rank4Body: Five consecutive ranks in mixed suits.
rank5Body: Five cards of one suit, not necessarily consecutive.
rank6Body: Three of a kind plus a pair. Compare the three of a kind first.
rank7Body: Four cards of the same rank and a kicker.
rank8Body: Five consecutive cards of the same suit.
rank9Body: 10, J, Q, K and A in one suit: the highest straight flush.
foldBody: You give up the hand; chips already committed stay in the pot.
checkBody: When there is nothing to call, stay in without adding chips.
callBody: Match the current bet up to the chips you have left.
betBody: Open betting on a street when no one has bet yet.
raiseBody: Increase the bet. “Raise to” is your total bet on this street, not just additional chips.
allinBody: Commit all remaining chips. It does not guarantee a win or let you win more from an opponent than you covered.
faq0Q: Do I need an account or money?
faq0A: No. Choose a nickname when playing. Chips and prizes are fictional; there are no deposits or withdrawals.
faq1Q: How do I play with bots?
faq1A: Create a room and add bots before dealing. The host chooses difficulty. Bots cannot see your cards.
faq2A: Use Copy invitation in room options. Share the password separately if the room is protected.
faq3Q: I closed the page. Did I lose my seat?
faq3A: Return using the same browser and link, keeping local data. A room is reserved for 30 minutes of absence after disconnection is detected. Choosing Leave ends your participation.
faq4Q: Why can’t I top up now?
faq4A: Top-ups happen only between hands under room limits and the rebuy window. Tournament rebuys require a zero stack.
faq5A: After up to one minute without human signals, play pauses. After 30 minutes of absence, the room expires. Bots do not extend the reservation.
faq6Q: How do I host a tournament?
faq6A: Choose Sit & Go for one table or Multi-table tournament. Set stacks, levels, breaks and rebuys. Invite players and start when ready. Balancing and virtual payouts are automatic.
faq7A: After a tournament, the podium and standings remain available for one hour. The host can export the public record without credentials or secret cards.

definition5: A tie-breaking card among the best five cards.
definition6: An additional forced contribution under room rules.
definition7: Entry in virtual chips under room rules.
definition8: A new chip entry when room rules allow it.

definition10: A separate pot when all-in players contribute different amounts.
